baseline_models.focus_anchor: The Form X request in word 1 is countered by the emphatic nominal predicate in word 5: they seek advancement of an event, while Hell is stated as encompassing them.
baseline_models.mechanism: The haste branch projects punishment as a punctual future arrival that can be pulled forward. The enclosure and overpowering branches of h-w-t instead make punishment a settled topology: delayed manifestation does not mean absent reach.

activation_trace.role: Speed, advancement, and asking before the due time supply the challengers' attempt to control when punishment appears.
Pain and punitive affliction identify the event they demand.
Physical encirclement turns the demanded event into a perimeter already holding its objects.
Overpowering enclosure ending in ruin gives that perimeter its punitive force.
Concealment and rejection of truth identify the people grammatically held inside the enclosure.

changed_reading.before: They ask for a future punishment, and the verse assures them that it will come.
changed_reading.after: Their request mistakes visibility for reach: they seek to advance a future manifestation while the emphatic nominal clause presents Hell's enclosure as already settled around the rejecters.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence muhitah bi-l-kafirin places an encompassing operation directly over a participial name whose root carries covering and concealment.
baseline_models.mechanism: K-f-r supplies both ordinary covering and the active concealment of truth; h-w-t reverses the direction of covering. Those characterized as coverers become the enclosed objects, so the clause stages a reflexive counter-cover rather than merely naming a target class.

activation_trace.role: Literal covering supplies the material image latent in the participial group name.
Concealing or rejecting truth specifies the group-defining use of that covering image.
Encircling with a wall redirects covering onto the coverers themselves.
An enclosure of overpowering ruin prevents the reversal from reading as protective cover.

changed_reading.before: Hell surrounds a doctrinally named group.
changed_reading.after: The wording also reverses the group's characteristic act: those who cover truth are themselves counter-covered by an overpowering enclosure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah first denies that wrongdoers can outdistance pursuit and announces a fixed term as coming. Immediately before the focus it repeats the haste request, locates arrival behind a named term, and makes manifestation sudden. The focus enclosure therefore distinguishes scheduled disclosure from present capture.

activation_trace.role: The focus perimeter supplies capture that need not wait for visible arrival.
Getting beyond a pursuer supplies the escape model that the ayah explicitly denies.
A fixed temporal limit supplies a schedule that comes independently of impatient demand.
The repeated request for advancement binds the immediate context to the focus's temporal challenge.
The exact punishment root appears both as requested object and as what would arrive at the appointed time.
The named endpoint blocks the challengers from setting punishment's timetable.
Sudden surprise marks the eventual perceptible crossing of a boundary already asserted in the focus.

structural_cues: 29:4 frames wrongdoing as a failed attempt to get ahead of divine pursuit.
29:5 places an announced coming under a fixed term long before the repeated challenge.
29:53 repeats the focus opening, then opposes appointed timing and sudden arrival to the challengers' lack of perception.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies race, fixed term, repeated haste, and surprise; I infer that nonappearance is scheduled concealment rather than escape and that 29:54 names the relation before it becomes perceptible. A live alternative is proleptic certainty about future Hell rather than a presently operative enclosure.

changed_reading.before: The enclosure is a forceful assurance that the punishment requested in 29:53 will eventually arrive.
changed_reading.after: Appointment governs when capture becomes manifest, not whether the challengers are within reach; the focus names an enclosure already defeating both haste and escape.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah unfolds the focus's circumference into a covering that closes the vertical axis from above and below, then converts spatial closure into embodied experience through tasting what was done. Enclosure becomes total contact rather than a distant ring.

activation_trace.role: Encirclement supplies the latent perimeter that the next ayah expands across further axes.
Punitive pain anchors the expanded spatial imagery in the focus's demanded punishment.
A covering that generally envelops supplies the transition from circumference to an all-over punitive layer.
The split root's second covering inventory independently reinforces concealment and total overlay.
Literal upper direction closes the enclosure overhead.
Literal underside closes the remaining vertical direction beneath their feet.
Experiencing and undergoing something converts geometry into personally verified contact.
Intentional deeds supply the conduct to which the tasted experience is explicitly related.

structural_cues: 29:55 follows the focus without a new addressee and specifies punishment from above and from beneath the feet.
Its command to taste shifts from third-person enclosure to second-person bodily verification.
The closing relative clause ties that verification to prior action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies enclosure, overlay, above/below directions, tasting, and deeds; I infer a feedback arrow in which conduct returns as the experienced enclosure. The live alternative is ordinary retributive correspondence, without deeds literally constituting its material.

changed_reading.before: Hell surrounds the rejecters as an abstract or lateral perimeter.
changed_reading.after: The focus is the latent perimeter of a closure that 29:55 renders overhead, underfoot, and bodily tasted, with no exposed direction remaining.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the surah, k-f-r changes grammatical object: God covers bad deeds away from believers; rejecters cover signs, gifts, and blessing; in the focus the coverers themselves become the object held by Hell. This makes the focus a reversal in who or what receives covering.

activation_trace.role: The generic covering image keeps the several root uses materially comparable.
Active concealment of truth identifies the focus's coverers rather than leaving kafirin a static label.
The focus enclosure makes those active coverers the receiving object of a counter-cover.
Erasing sin by covering it supplies the benevolent polarity: bad deeds, not persons, are covered away from believers.
Rejection of disclosed signs activates kafirun as an ongoing concealment relation.
Covering a received gift turns ingratitude into one explicit object of the rejecters' action.
Concealing blessing sharpens that action immediately before Hell and the kafirin recur in 29:68.

structural_cues: 29:7 directs k-f-r toward believers' bad deeds and away from their persons.
29:47 predicates rejection of signs only of the kafirun.
29:66-67 direct k-f-r toward what was given and toward God's blessing, while 29:54 makes the kafirin themselves the complement of encompassing Hell.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated root and its changing objects; I infer a reciprocal arrow in which chosen covering returns as enclosure of the coverers. The live alternative is a contrast among ordinary polysemous uses with no causal reversal intended.

changed_reading.before: Kafirin is simply the class on whom Hell's punishment falls.
changed_reading.after: The class is dynamically defined by what it covers, and the focus reverses that relation: unlike believers whose evils are covered away, these coverers become what the enclosing fire covers.

context_deltas.mechanism: The spider comparison exposes a chosen protective house as structurally weak; the closing challenge names Hell as the settled dwelling of the same kafirin. Between them, the focus's encompassing predicate functions as the conversion point from failed self-chosen shelter to inescapable imposed abode.

activation_trace.role: A surrounding wall supplies the holding structure that links shelter and confinement.
The focus group is the same truth-rejecting class for whom the later dwelling is named.
The repeated house as refuge or dwelling supplies the self-chosen protective structure.
Weakness of force makes that adopted refuge unable to hold or protect.
A settled lodging or dwelling turns Hell from a passing strike into the place that actually holds its occupants.
The repeated kafirin explicitly assigns that forced abode to the focus's enclosed group.

structural_cues: 29:41 compares adopted protectors to a spider taking a house and repeats that this is the weakest house.
29:68 closes with a rhetorical question naming a mathwa in Hell for the kafirin.
The focus places an emphatic encompassing predicate between the failed-house image and the final dwelling.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies weak chosen shelter, encompassing Hell, and a final assigned dwelling; I infer an inversion from attempted refuge to forced habitation. A live alternative is that the spider house and Hell abode are independent images sharing only the broad domain of dwelling.

changed_reading.before: Hell's enclosure is a spatial threat surrounding individuals.
changed_reading.after: It is also the only dwelling that successfully holds: failed chosen shelters give way to an imposed abode whose enclosing structure cannot fail.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the form-distant premature-birth branch of a-j-l. It remains anchored in the exact haste verb and is sharpened by the surah's repeated fixed ajal; downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for forcing an outcome before its term, not as a claim that the ayah explicitly invokes childbirth.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The challengers use the a-j-l haste form, while the focus counters them with an enclosure already in force rather than granting an early visible outcome.

activation_trace.role: Delivery before full term supplies an embodied image for demanding that punishment emerge before its appointed maturation.
Existing enclosure keeps the delayed outcome from being mistaken for a process not yet underway.
The fixed temporal endpoint supplies the due term against which premature advancement is imagined.
The verbatim repeated haste request carries the premature-delivery image into the immediate lead-in.
The named deadline immediately opposes forcing the punitive outcome before its due point.

changed_reading.before: They impatiently ask for punishment to be accelerated.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, they demand premature delivery of an outcome whose term is fixed; 29:54 answers that delayed emergence does not mean the enclosing process is absent.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads the secure sanctuary and the danger around it as a scale model for the focus's larger unseen perimeter. It remains anchored in h-w-t enclosure and the repeated k-f-r relation, but downstream prose must qualify the nesting as a spatial analogy and must not identify the sanctuary itself with Hell.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus joins encompassing h-w-t to kafirin; 29:67 juxtaposes a protected center, snatching around it, and active covering of blessing.

activation_trace.role: Encirclement supplies the larger perimeter into which the local protected zone can be analogically nested.
Truth-covering anchors the nested image in the exact group enclosed by Hell.
A bounded sanctuary supplies the protected inner perimeter.
Swift snatching supplies the danger operating immediately outside that protected center.
The direction around a thing explicitly maps danger onto the sanctuary's surrounding zone.
Covering the blessing of local security explains how an inner refuge can obscure awareness of the larger punitive horizon.

changed_reading.before: Hell surrounds the rejecters in a single undifferentiated space.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, present security is a small protected perimeter inside a larger unseen enclosure; covering the inner blessing helps hide the outer horizon already around the coverers.

strongest_changes: The requested future event became a distinction between appointed manifestation and already-established capture.
The next ayah expanded circumference into covering from above and below, then into bodily tasting related to deeds.
Repeated k-f-r uses reversed the object of covering: believers' evils are covered away, while the coverers of signs and blessing are themselves enclosed.
The spider house and final mathwa changed enclosure from a passing threat into an imposed dwelling that succeeds where chosen refuges fail.
summary.what_was_special: The emphatic nominal muhitah sits between the verbatim request in 29:53 and the above/below covering in 29:55, allowing temporal delay, spatial closure, and lexical covering to reverse one another without collapsing into one reading.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether muhitah marks a presently operative enclosure or proleptic certainty about future Hell.
Whether the k-f-r object reversal is a designed mechanism or productive lexical resonance.
Whether tasting what was done implies deeds constituting the enclosure or only ordinary recompense.
Whether the nested-sanctuary and premature-delivery images should survive beyond exploratory prose.
